memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Eleazar son of Aaron married one of the daughters of Putiel, and she bore him Phinehas. These were the heads of the Levite families, clan by clan. It was this Aaron and Moses to whom the Lord said, "Bring the Israelites out of Egypt by their divisions." They were the ones who spoke to Pharaoh king of Egypt about bringing the Israelites out of Egypt. It was the same Moses and Aaron." - Exodus 6:25-27 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The passage ends by underlining something almost with a raised voice: it was the same Moses and Aaron.

Why insist on it? Because it would be easy for later readers to imagine these men as legends — larger-than-life figures who were somehow made of different material. The text refuses. The men who confronted the most powerful king on earth were these men, from this family, with these ordinary relatives.

The same Moses who stammered. The same Aaron who would one day make a golden calf. Same men.

God's heroes are never a separate species. James makes the same point about Elijah — he was a human being just like us, and he prayed (Jas 5:17).

That cuts both ways. It removes our excuse that we are too ordinary to be used. And it removes our pride if God ever does use us, because we know exactly what we are made of.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I let admiration for others become an excuse for my own inaction?
2. If God used me, would I remember what I am actually made of?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You use ordinary people. Keep me from both false humility and quiet pride. Amen.
